asks: Asks for one more Edmonton seat and for Larkspur to be kept in Edmonton-Meadows.
Supports the interim Edmonton-South West and Edmonton-West-Enoch ridings and asks that Enoch Cree Nation be consulted.
Asks that Edmonton-Rutherford keep its current boundaries rather than extend south to Ellerslie Road.
Asks the commission to account for an undercount of post-secondary students in the 2021 census in Edmonton-Strathcona, Riverview and Gold Bar.
Asks for one riding called Sherwood Park, extended to Highway 21 including Heritage Hills, and questions Beaumont's inclusion in Strathcona-Sherwood Park.
Asks for an additional seat for Edmonton.
Asks for an additional Edmonton seat and for Ritchie to stay in Edmonton-Strathcona, using Mill Creek Ravine as the boundary.
No specific request; urges fairness and communities of interest and warns against rural ridings that take in pieces of cities.

note: Ronaghan's words 'Certainly, areas like Lesser Slave Lake are way below the other areas in Edmonton' appear, through reading-order bleed, inside the text of HANSARD-R2-T40-008 (EB-678), not in this record. Named as an example of a low-population riding; no request (rule 6).

asks: Asks that Heritage Hills stay in Strathcona-Sherwood Park and that Beaumont and Leduc County not be added to it.
Supports Edmonton-Glenora-Riverview and Edmonton-West-Enoch and asks for two boundary corrections to Stony Plain-Drayton Valley-Devon near Calmar and Holborn.
Asks for another Edmonton seat and for Ritchie to be returned to Edmonton-Strathcona; offers the Western Arctic as a model for the large interim Mackenzie riding without asking for a change there.

note: Names the interim riding 72 Mackenzie (the district that absorbed Lesser Slave Lake) and expresses 'some sympathy' about its size, but never names Lesser Slave Lake and asks for nothing about keeping or dissolving it; offers the NWT federal riding as a comparison. Narrow reading (rule 17).

asks: Supports the interim Sherwood Park map (Heritage Hills included) and asks that Strathcona-Sherwood Park be renamed, e.g. Beaver Hills or Ardrossan.

Asks the commission to keep the interim seat distribution, not remove an Edmonton seat, move the Spruce Avenue neighbourhood into Edmonton-Highlands-Norwood, and keep Edmonton seats inside city limits.

note: Says 'I support the decision, as painful as it was, to remove a seat from northern Alberta. That's what the numbers warrant.' in reply to the Chair's reference to the north's cry to 'restore the riding you took away'. The interim seat removed was Lesser Slave Lake, but he never names it or any district; coded as a mention without a want (rules 1 and 17). A broad reading would be want K2.

asks: Supports the interim changes to Edmonton-McClung (Willowby, Wedgewood Heights, Rio Terrace, Quesnell, Patricia Heights) and asks for one more Edmonton seat.
Supports the interim plan, including two-seat Lethbridge and Edmonton as its own community of interest, asks that Edmonton's added seat be preserved, and urges population parity.

quote: I greatly appreciate the commission’s decision on Lethbridge. There’s sort of a bizarre proposal to slice that up in a funny way, and that obviously isn’t in this interim plan.
note: Supports the interim two-city-seat Lethbridge; calls the proposal to 'slice that up' bizarre (the hearing-round proposal of the four-way hybrid kind; the particulars are not described, so the rejection of L2 is by inference). Passage comes before the first EB label in the record (EB-691), so the record's PDF page range is given.

asks: Asks for a seat to be added to Edmonton, for Glenora and Riverview to be left as is with a hybrid added on the outskirts, and voices concern about losing Lesser Slave Lake.

quote: I have concerns about the loss of the constituency in Lesser Slave Lake. Those are communities of interest.
note: Said in passing, in answer to Mr. Clark's question about hybrids; objection to the interim dissolution translated into a want for the riding (rule 4).

asks: Asks the commission to recognize densification in Edmonton-Glenora-Riverview, which is already over-populated, and suggests another seat between the Yellowhead and the Whitemud.

Asks that central Alberta keep its rural seats, that Sylvan Lake go to the Lacombe riding, and that Innisfail join the Highway 2 and Highway 21 corridor towns (Bowden, Penhold, Blackfalds, Delburne, Elnora, Huxley, Trochu) in a new riding.

quote: I believe that those MLAs that share the city and the rural area around it are richer for that experience. I believe in the hub-andspoke concept of it.
note: Closing remark drawn from his federal experience of representing Red Deer city with the county; endorses 'hub-and-spoke' city-and-country ridings in general but his concrete proposal (Sylvan Lake with Lacombe; Innisfail with the corridor towns) asks nothing about joining any part of the City of Red Deer. Broad reading would be R2 at direction; narrower reading kept (rule 17). Also says a Sylvan Lake-Red Deer boundary is 'something that one can take a look at' (rule 8: no request).

quote: the towns, villages, and hamlets along the highway 21 corridor of Joffre, Delburne, Lousana, Elnora, Huxley, and Trochu should be included in a new riding
note: Wants Trochu and Huxley (Kneehill County) taken into a new Innisfail-centred corridor riding, rather than in the prairie Olds/Kneehill riding of O1 or O2. Says nothing about Sundre, Crossfield, Irricana, Beiseker or Mountain View County. Dr. Martin presses him on including Trochu and he defends it.

asks: Asks for another Edmonton seat in view of growth in Edmonton-North West and the other most populous Edmonton ridings.

quote: God bless the proposed Mackenzie. I think that’s a fantastic idea. I really do.
note: Names the interim Mackenzie riding (which absorbed Lesser Slave Lake) while comparing its population with Edmonton-North West; the remark's tone is unclear (it could be ironic) and Lesser Slave Lake is never named. Broad reading would be want K2; narrower reading kept (rules 1 and 17).
